mainTopic: דם טוהר and the rule of סתם ואחר כך מחלוקת; when a young bride's blood counts as pure; and when a woman must check herself before intercourse.
overview: The גמרא first explains that the משנה's exemption from checking for a woman sitting on דם טוהר follows בית שמאי. It defends this with the rule סתם ואחר כך מחלוקת אין הלכה כסתם. A second answer says the משנה speaks of a woman already sitting on דם טוהר. It teaches that a וסת does not carry over from the pure days to the impure days, and this holds even for רב, who says there is one source. Next the גמרא turns to the virgin whose blood is pure. It brings the משנה about a young bride, where בית שמאי give her four nights and בית הלל say until the wound heals. שמואל lists the signs that her blood is no longer pure: the bleeding with intercourse stopped, a night passed without intercourse, or the color changed. The גמרא settles רבי יונה's challenge by splitting the case into whether or not she had intercourse, and a ברייתא supports שמואל. Finally, שמואל rules that the check before intercourse applies only to a woman who handles טהרות. After several challenges, a ברייתא confirms this and adds that it holds only if her husband left her presumed pure.

steps.title: The author of the rule is בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier question by saying the משנה's rule follows בית שמאי, who hold that both kinds of blood come from one source.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the view of בית שמאי, who say that there is only one source for both kinds of blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question raised just before this, about why the משנה does not require a check. It does so by naming who wrote the rule: בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that the blood of the impure days and the blood of the pure days come from one single source. On that view, the check the previous question asked for is not needed. So the משנה's exemption fits their opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Source (literally 'spring'), meaning the place in the body the blood comes from
One source, meaning both kinds of blood come from the same place
Blood seen during the days after childbirth when the Torah treats it as pure

phrases.english: It is the view of Beit Shammai,
who say: it is one source.
phrases.notes: Their view appears in the משנה on 35b.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this part of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the author of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's exemption from checking seemed hard to explain.
steps.terutzMaskana: It follows בית שמאי, who hold there is one source for both kinds of blood.

steps.title: Would an unnamed משנה follow בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised that an unnamed משנה would follow בית שמאי, since the הלכה usually follows בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But would the תנא teach us an unnamed ruling that follows בית שמאי?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. An unnamed משנה is normally the accepted הלכה, so how could it follow בית שמאי?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two rules in the background. First, a סתם משנה, an unnamed ruling, usually shows us the הלכה. Second, we almost never rule like בית שמאי against בית הלל. Putting the two together, it seems strange that רבי would state בית שמאי's view without a name.

keyTerms.meaning: An unnamed ruling in the משנה, which is usually the accepted הלכה
The teacher of the משנה (here, the one who arranged it)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is questioning בית שמאי's opinion itself. The question is only why the משנה would state their view without a name, as if it were the הלכה.

phrases.english: And the tanna taught us an unattributed ruling like Beit Shammai?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: Saying the unnamed משנה follows בית שמאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unnamed משנה stands for the הלכה, and the הלכה does not follow בית שמאי, so the משנה should not follow them.

steps.title: An unnamed ruling followed by a dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this unnamed ruling is later followed by a dispute, and in such a case the הלכה does not have to follow the unnamed ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a case of an unnamed ruling that is followed later by a dispute. Whenever an unnamed ruling is followed later by a dispute, the הלכה does not follow the unnamed ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its answer. The same issue shows up later as an open dispute (on 35b), so the unnamed ruling here does not count as the final הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unnamed ruling usually carries great weight. But when the משנה later shows the very same question as a dispute between named opinions, the unnamed version loses that special status. So it is fine for this unnamed line to follow בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: An unnamed ruling that is followed later by a dispute on the same issue
The הלכה does not follow the unnamed ruling

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule for deciding הלכה from the משנה, and it is used throughout ש״ס.
steps.whatToRemember: An unnamed משנה usually tells us the הלכה. But if a dispute on the same issue appears later, that weight is lost: סתם ואחר כך מחלוקת אין הלכה כסתם.

phrases.english: It is an unattributed ruling and afterward a dispute,
phrases.notes: The dispute it means is the one between בית שמאי and בית הלל on 35b.

phrases.english: and any unattributed ruling followed afterward by a dispute,
the halakha is not like the unattributed ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general rule about how to decide הלכה from the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An unnamed משנה is always the final הלכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because a dispute follows later, this unnamed ruling is not the binding הלכה, so it may follow בית שמאי.

steps.title: Second answer: she is already sitting
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the משנה speaks of a woman who is already sitting on דם טוהר, not one who is about to begin.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: does the משנה say 'wants to sit'? It says 'is sitting'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different answer to the original question. It reads the משנה's wording carefully: it speaks of a woman who is already in her pure days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer needed the view of בית שמאי. This answer works for everyone. Since the woman is already in the pure days, the worry about the switch from impure days to pure days does not apply at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead (brings a second answer)
Wants to sit, meaning about to begin her pure days
Is sitting, meaning already in the middle of her pure days

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Does it teach 'wanting to sit'?
It teaches 'is sitting'!
phrases.notes: The משנה's words are 'חוץ מיושבת על דם טוהר', meaning except for a woman sitting on pure blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא מִי קָתָנֵי מְבַקֶּשֶׁת לֵישֵׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer, in place of steps 1-3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A careful reading of the משנה's words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה was thought to speak of a woman just starting her pure days.
steps.terutzMaskana: It speaks of a woman already sitting, so the check at the switch does not apply.

steps.title: Then why does it need to be said?
steps.stepSummary: If she is already sitting on דם טוהר, it seems obvious that she does not need to check, so why does the משנה say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If she is already sitting, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the second answer. If the woman is already in her pure days, the exemption seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the pure days, any blood she sees is pure anyway, so a check seems to serve no purpose. The משנה must therefore be teaching something new, and the גמרא wants to know what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the point of saying it? (meaning: isn't it obvious?)

phrases.english: If she is sitting, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second answer of step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the משנה as speaking of a woman already sitting
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she is already in her pure days, the exemption from checking is obvious, so the משנה would have nothing to teach.

steps.title: No cycle from a pure source to an impure source
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed: one might think she should check in case she is setting a וסת, but a וסת is not set from a pure source to an impure source.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said she should check, since perhaps she is setting a fixed cycle. So the משנה teaches us that a cycle is not set from a pure source to an impure source.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the משנה teaches. We might have thought she should check during her pure days in order to keep track of a possible fixed cycle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood seen during the pure days could in theory create a pattern, a וסת, that would matter later when she is in impure days. The משנה tells us that such a pattern does not carry over from pure blood to impure blood. So there is no reason to check.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken idea)
It teaches us (introduces the new lesson)
A fixed menstrual cycle or pattern
She set, meaning she established a pattern

phrases.english: Lest you say she should examine herself,
since perhaps she is establishing a fixed cycle —
it teaches us

phrases.aramaic: דְּמַעְיָן טָהוֹר לְמַעְיָן טָמֵא לָא קָבְעָה.
phrases.english: that from a pure source to an impure source she does not establish a cycle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the new lesson in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She should check during her pure days in case a וסת is being set.
steps.terutzMaskana: A וסת is not set from a pure source to an impure source, so no check is needed.

steps.title: This works for לוי, but what about רב?
steps.stepSummary: The answer fits לוי, who holds there are two separate sources. But רב holds there is one source, so on his view she should check.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to לוי, who said there are two sources. But according to רב, who said there is one source, she should check, since perhaps she is setting a fixed cycle!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 6. It works only if pure and impure blood come from different sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 talked about a 'pure source' and an 'impure source,' which fits לוי's view of two separate sources. רב holds there is only one source. If so, blood from the pure days really comes from the same place as impure blood, and it should be able to set a וסת.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (for one opinion, but not for another)
Two separate sources for the two kinds of blood

phrases.english: This works well according to Levi, who said:
they are two sources,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַב דְּאָמַר: מַעְיָן אֶחָד הוּא —
phrases.english: but according to Rav, who said: it is one source —
she should examine herself, as perhaps she is establishing a fixed cycle!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְלֵוִי דְּאָמַר שְׁנֵי מַעְיָנוֹת הֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a וסת is not set from a pure source to an impure source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רב there is only one source, so pure-day blood should be able to set a וסת, and a check would be needed.

steps.title: Even with one source, no carryover
steps.stepSummary: Even according to רב, a וסת does not carry over from the days of purity to the days of impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, a cycle is not set from the days of purity to the days of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule holds even for רב. What blocks the carryover is the difference between the two periods of days, not where the blood comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer moves the reason. It is no longer 'different sources.' Now it is 'different periods of time.' Even if all the blood comes from one place, a pattern seen in the pure days does not set a וסת for the impure days.

keyTerms.meaning: Even so
The days of purity after childbirth
The days of impurity

steps.whatToRemember: A woman sitting on דם טוהר does not need to check, because a וסת does not carry over from the pure days to the impure days. This is true according to both לוי and רב.

phrases.english: Even so,

phrases.aramaic: מִימֵי טׇהֳרָה לִימֵי טוּמְאָה לָא קָבְעָה.
phrases.english: from the days of purity to the days of impurity she does not establish a cycle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving a new reason for the same rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No carryover happens only because there are two separate sources.
steps.terutzMaskana: No carryover happens because the days are different, which is true even if there is one source.

steps.title: Quoting the next words of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves on to the next words of the משנה: a woman uses examination cloths during intercourse.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And she uses examination cloths during intercourse,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a woman uses examination cloths during intercourse, except for a woman sitting on דם טוהר and a virgin whose blood is pure. The גמרא is about to explain the exception about a virgin, so it starts by quoting this line.

keyTerms.meaning: Has marital relations
Examination cloths used to check for blood (literally 'witnesses')
And so on: the rest of the line is not quoted

phrases.english: And she engages in intercourse with examination cloths, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the line is 'except for a woman sitting on דם טוהר and a virgin whose blood is pure'. The גמרא is about to discuss the virgin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section after finishing the topic of דם טוהר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman uses examination cloths during intercourse, except in certain cases such as a virgin.

steps.title: A young bride: four nights or until the wound heals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה about a young girl who marries before she is old enough to menstruate. בית שמאי give her four nights, and בית הלל say until the wound heals.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: a young girl who has not yet reached the age of seeing blood and got married: בית שמאי say they give her four nights, and בית הלל say until the wound heals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related משנה (from 64b) to help explain the 'virgin' exception. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a girl this young, blood after her wedding is assumed to come from the wound of first intercourse, so it is pure. The dispute is about how long that assumption lasts. בית שמאי say a fixed four nights, while בית הלל say as long as the wound has not healed.

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl
Who has not yet reached the age of seeing menstrual blood
Four nights during which her blood is treated as pure
Until the wound heals

steps.confusionAlert: Here בית הלל are actually the more lenient side: they give her as long as the wound takes to heal, which can be more than four nights.

phrases.english: We learned there:

phrases.aramaic: תִּינוֹקֶת שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּהּ לִרְאוֹת וְנִשֵּׂאת,
phrases.english: A young girl whose time to see has not arrived, and she married,
Beit Shammai say:
we give her four nights,
phrases.notes: During those nights her blood is treated as coming from the wound, so she stays pure.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say:
until the wound heals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related משנה to explain the 'virgin' exception quoted in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a young bride, בית שמאי allow four nights of pure blood, and בית הלל allow it until the wound heals.

steps.title: שמואל limits בית הלל's leniency
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the bride's blood counts as pure wound-blood only while bleeding keeps coming with intercourse. If that bleeding has stopped and she later sees blood, she is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of שמואל: בית הלל only meant this when her bleeding with intercourse has not stopped, and she then saw blood not from intercourse. But if the bleeding with intercourse stopped and she then saw blood, she is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains the limits of בית הלל's rule that a young bride's blood is pure 'until the wound heals.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל did not say how we know the wound has healed. שמואל gives a sign: as long as every act of intercourse still brings blood, the wound is still open, so even other blood is blamed on it. Once intercourse no longer brings blood, the wound has healed, and any new blood is regular impure blood.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when... (a way of narrowing an earlier ruling)
She stopped (seeing blood)
Because of intercourse
Impure

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Shmuel said:
They only taught this
phrases.notes: 'This' is בית הלל's rule from the last step, that her blood is pure until the wound heals.

phrases.english: where she did not stop bleeding from intercourse,
and she saw blood not from intercourse;
but if she stopped bleeding from intercourse and then saw blood —
she is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows בית הלל's ruling from the משנה quoted in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood is pure only while intercourse still brings bleeding; once that stops, later blood makes her impure.

steps.title: Two more signs that the wound has healed
steps.stepSummary: שמואל adds two more cases where she is impure: a night passed with no intercourse and she then saw blood, or the color of her blood changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one night passed with no intercourse and she then saw blood, she is impure. If the look of her blood changed, she is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל continues his ruling and gives two more signs that the blood is no longer from the wound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wound-blood comes with intercourse, so blood after a night with no intercourse does not look like wound-blood. And wound-blood keeps the same look, so a change in color shows it is a new kind of blood.

keyTerms.meaning: One night passed
Changed
The look (color) of the blood

phrases.english: If one night passed without intercourse
and she saw blood — she is impure.
If the look of her blood changed —
she is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues שמואל's statement with more cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood after a night with no intercourse, or blood that changed color, makes her impure.

steps.title: רבי יונה: then why doesn't she check?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה challenges the color-change rule. The משנה says a virgin with pure blood does not use examination cloths, but if a color change matters, she should check.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונה objected: The משנה says 'and a virgin whose blood is pure' does not use cloths. Why not? Let her use examination cloths during intercourse, because maybe the look of her blood has changed!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונה attacks שמואל's last rule using the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (step 9) lists a virgin whose blood is pure among women who do not need to check with cloths. If a change in color makes her impure, as שמואל says, she would need to check for it. So the משנה seems to go against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: A virgin whose blood is pure (the young bride with wound-blood)
She should have intercourse using examination cloths
Because perhaps

phrases.english: Rabbi Yona raised an objection:
"And a virgin whose blood is pure" (does not use cloths).
Why? Let her have intercourse using examination cloths,
because maybe the look of her blood has changed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the color-change rule of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a change in the blood's color makes her impure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a color change matters, the משנה should require her to check, yet it says she does not.

steps.title: רבא: the first clause supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רבא points to the first clause of the same משנה. It exempts only a נדה and a woman sitting on דם טוהר, which suggests a virgin with pure blood does need to check.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Look at the first clause: 'except for a נדה and a woman sitting on דם טוהר.' Only they do not need checking, but a virgin whose blood is pure does need checking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רבי יונה by showing that another part of the same משנה actually fits שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause gives a list of who does not need cloths, and the virgin is not on it. That implies she does need to check, which matches שמואל's worry about a color change. So the משנה cannot simply be used against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (look at) the first clause
A woman who is already impure from her period
A woman after childbirth in the days when her blood is pure
Needs checking

phrases.english: Rava said: Look at the first clause:
"Except for a menstruating woman
and one who is sitting on blood of purity" —
it is they who do not need checking,
but a virgin whose blood is pure
does need checking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on רבי יונה's objection by using another clause of the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that she must watch for a change in her blood's color.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first clause of the משנה, which leaves the virgin off the list of women who don't need checking.

steps.title: The two clauses contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: Now the משנה seems to argue with itself: the first clause implies a virgin must check, and the later clause says she need not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then the two clauses are difficult against each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that, after רבא's reading, the two parts of the משנה clash. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונה's clause says the virgin doesn't check, and רבא's clause implies she does. Both can't be true in the same case, so the גמרא needs to find two different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: They contradict each other

phrases.english: But then they contradict each other!
phrases.notes: 'They' are the two clauses of the משנה: the one רבי יונה quoted and the one רבא quoted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts the clause from step 13 against the inference from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the משנה itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One clause implies a virgin must check and the other says she need not.

steps.title: Two cases: after intercourse and without it
steps.stepSummary: The clause that exempts her is about a case where she had intercourse, since any color change could be blamed on the man's organ. The clause that requires checking is about a case with no intercourse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, it is where she had intercourse, since we can say the organ dirtied the blood. There, it is where she did not have intercourse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by placing each clause in a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she checks with cloths during intercourse and the color looks different, it proves nothing, because the intercourse itself could have dirtied the blood. So checking then is useless, and the virgin is exempt. When there was no intercourse, a color change is a real sign, so she must check, just as שמואל said.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there (each source is about a different case)
She had intercourse
A polite word for the male organ
Made them murky / dirtied them

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: the bride's blood is pure only while intercourse still brings bleeding, no night passes without it before she sees blood, and the color stays the same. She checks for a color change only when there was no intercourse, because after intercourse a change could just come from the intercourse itself.

phrases.english: Here — where she had intercourse,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the clause רבי יונה quoted, which says she doesn't use cloths.

phrases.english: since one can say the organ made the blood murky;
there — where she did not have intercourse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses seemed to be about the same situation, so they looked like they contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exemption applies when she had intercourse, since checking can't prove anything then. The requirement to check applies when she did not, which fits שמואל.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל's cases of impurity
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same thing as שמואל. A virgin's blood is pure only while she keeps bleeding from intercourse. If the bleeding stopped, a night passed without intercourse, or the color changed, she is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same: When is she pure? Only when her bleeding from intercourse has not stopped, and then she sees blood even not from intercourse. But if the bleeding from intercourse stopped and she then sees blood, she is impure. If one night passed with no intercourse and she saw blood, she is impure. If the color of her blood changed, she is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what שמואל said, so it supports him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a virgin's blood is pure applies only while it still looks like it comes from the wound of the first intercourse. The ברייתא lists the same three cases that break this assumption: the bleeding stopped, a night passed without intercourse, or the color changed. In each case we can no longer blame the wound, so she is טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? (introduces a limit on a rule)
She stopped (bleeding)
Because of intercourse
Impure (she is a נדה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This confirms the color-change rule that רבי יונה challenged in Step 13 and the גמרא defended in Steps 14 to 16.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא:
In what case is this said?
phrases.notes: This refers to the rule that a newly married virgin's blood is treated as pure, coming from the wound.

phrases.english: Where she has not stopped bleeding from intercourse,
and she saw blood not from intercourse.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל פָּסְקָה מֵחֲמַת תַּשְׁמִישׁ וְרָאֲתָה — טְמֵאָה,
phrases.english: But if she stopped bleeding from intercourse and then saw blood, she is impure.
If one night passed without intercourse
and she saw blood, she is impure.
If the color of her blood changed, she is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the color-change rule was defended, a ברייתא is brought that states all of שמואל's cases.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's list of cases where a virgin's blood is impure
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same three cases

steps.title: שמואל limits the twice-daily check to pure items
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's rule that a woman checks herself twice a day, שמואל says this is only for handling pure items. For her husband, she is permitted without it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'She must check herself twice a day,' etc. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This was taught only for pure items. But she is permitted to her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, and שמואל explains who that rule is for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a woman checks herself twice a day, in the morning and at dusk. שמואל says these checks protect pure items (טהרות) she might touch. They are not needed for her to be with her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. (the rest of the line of the משנה)
They only taught this for... (limits a rule)
Pure items (food or objects kept in purity)
Permitted to her husband

phrases.english: The משנה said: 'She needs to check twice,' etc.
phrases.notes: The full line: she checks in the morning and at dusk, and also before intercourse.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
They taught this only for pure items,
but she is permitted to her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּעֲמַיִם הִיא צְרִיכָה וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the next line of the משנה, about examinations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The twice-daily checks are only for טהרות. She needs no such check to be permitted to her husband.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious from the word 'morning'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל needed to say this. The משנה says the check is in the morning, which clearly is about pure items.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! We learned 'in the morning.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל: his point seems to add nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה places the first check in the morning. A morning check fits the purity of things she will handle during the day, not intercourse. So the משנה already shows it is about טהרות, and שמואל's statement seems unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (why say it?)
In the morning

phrases.english: That is obvious!
We learned 'in the morning'!
phrases.notes: A morning check is plainly about pure items for the day ahead, not about being with her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's statement as saying something the משנה already makes clear.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that the twice-daily check is only for טהרות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'morning' in the משנה already shows the check is about pure items, so the statement is unnecessary.

steps.title: שמואל was really talking about the check before intercourse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves שמואל's statement to the later clause, the check before intercourse. Only a woman who handles pure items must do that check.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, it was said on the later clause: 'and when she is about to be with her husband.' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This was taught only about a woman who handles pure items. Since she needs a check for pure items, she also needs a check for her husband. But a woman who does not handle pure items does not need a check.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by saying שמואל's statement was really on the next part of the משנה, and it restates what he said there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה also requires a check before intercourse. שמואל says this applies only to a woman who already checks for טהרות. Since she checks anyway, the check covers her husband too (מגו). A woman who does not handle pure items does not need this check at all.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said (introduces where a statement really belongs)
The later clause of the משנה
To be intimate with her husband
A woman who handles pure items
Since (since this is true here, it is also true there)

steps.whatToRemember: The check before intercourse is required only of a woman who handles טהרות. A woman who does not handle pure items does not need to check before being with her husband.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל's words are not about the morning and dusk checks. The גמרא moved them to the check before intercourse.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, it was said on the later clause:

phrases.aramaic: וּבְשָׁעָה שֶׁהִיא עוֹבֶרֶת לְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת בֵּיתָהּ.
phrases.english: 'And when she is about to be with her husband.'
רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּאִשָּׁה עֲסוּקָה בִּטְהָרוֹת,
phrases.english: They taught this only about a woman who handles pure items,
since she needs a check for pure items,
she also needs a check for her husband.
But a woman who does not handle pure items
does not need a check.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' objection by placing שמואל's statement on a different clause of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the statement to a different clause of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל was talking about the morning and dusk checks, which would make his point obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל was talking about the check before intercourse. Only a woman who handles טהרות needs it, because of מגו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The check before intercourse applies only to a woman who handles pure items.

steps.title: Why did שמואל need to say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל's ruling adds, since a משנה already teaches that all women are presumed pure for their husbands.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned: All women are presumed pure for their husbands!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's ruling from Step 20. It looks like it repeats something a משנה already says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said a woman who does not handle pure items needs no check before intercourse. But a משנה already says every woman is presumed pure for her husband. So שמואל seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asks what a statement adds)
a presumption of purity; we assume she is pure unless we know otherwise
their husbands

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned:
All women are presumed pure for their husbands!
phrases.notes: This is a different משנה, found later in the מסכת (15a).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of שמואל as placed in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that only a woman handling pure items must check before intercourse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already says all women are presumed pure for their husbands, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Without שמואל, we would limit the משנה to a woman with a fixed cycle
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה alone we might think only a woman with a fixed cycle is presumed pure. שמואל teaches that a woman without one is also exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had the משנה, I would have said this applies only to a woman with a fixed cycle. But a woman without a fixed cycle would need a check.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל does add something new. Without him, we would have said a woman with no fixed cycle must check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman with a וסת knows roughly when her period comes, so it makes sense to assume she is pure at other times. A woman without a וסת has no such timing, so we might have required a check. שמואל teaches that even she is exempt, unless she handles pure items.

keyTerms.meaning: a fixed menstrual cycle, a set pattern for when her period comes
an internal check to see whether she is pure
I would have said (what we might wrongly think)

phrases.english: If we only had the משנה, I would have said

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּאִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת,
phrases.english: this applies only to a woman who has a fixed cycle,
but a woman who has no fixed cycle
needs a check.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement adds a new case: a woman without a fixed cycle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a woman with a fixed cycle is presumed pure. A woman without one must check.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a woman without a fixed cycle may be with her husband without a check, unless she handles pure items.

steps.title: But our משנה is about a woman with a fixed cycle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that our משנה, which שמואל was explaining, speaks of a woman who has a fixed cycle.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in our משנה we are dealing with a woman who has a fixed cycle!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 22. שמואל was explaining our משנה, and that משנה is about a woman with a fixed cycle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said שמואל teaches a law about a woman without a fixed cycle. But שמואל's words sit on our משנה, which talks about a woman who has one. So how can his ruling be about a woman without one?

keyTerms.meaning: we are dealing with (the case under discussion)

phrases.english: But our משנה,
phrases.notes: This means our משנה, the one שמואל was commenting on, not the משנה quoted in Step 21.

phrases.english: we are dealing with a woman who has a fixed cycle!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מַתְנִיתִין בְּאִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמואל's ruling is about a woman without a fixed cycle.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל was explaining our משנה, and that משנה is about a woman who has a fixed cycle.

steps.title: Our משנה covers both kinds of women
steps.stepSummary: The משנה includes women with and without a fixed cycle. It teaches that a woman with a fixed cycle who handles pure items must check before intercourse too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is about both a woman with a fixed cycle and a woman without one. It teaches us that even a woman with a fixed cycle, since she must check for pure items, must also check for her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our משנה covers both kinds of women. It also explains what the משנה adds for a woman with a fixed cycle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה includes a woman with no fixed cycle, שמואל can be speaking about her too. For a woman with a fixed cycle, the משנה adds a new point. If she handles pure items, she must check for those anyway, so she must also check before being with her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: since (one law is true, a related law follows)
pure items, food or objects kept in a state of ritual purity
even though

phrases.english: Our משנה is about both where she has a fixed cycle
and where she has no fixed cycle,
and this is what it teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּיֵשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת,
phrases.english: that even though she has a fixed cycle,
since she needs a check for pure items,
she also needs a check for her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין בֵּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת, בֵּין אֵין לָהּ וֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widens the case of the משנה to include both kinds of women.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה speaks only of a woman with a fixed cycle.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה covers both kinds of women. A woman who handles pure items must check before intercourse, even if she has a fixed cycle.

steps.title: Did שמואל say the same thing twice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that שמואל already gave a similar ruling: a woman without a fixed cycle may not have intercourse until she checks. That ruling was explained as being about a woman who handles pure items.
steps.simpleTranslation: But שמואל already said this once! For רבי זירא said that רבי אבא בר ירמיה said that שמואל said: A woman with no fixed cycle may not have intercourse until she checks. And we explained that as a woman who handles pure items!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second statement of שמואל that seems to say the same thing. It asks why he would repeat himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other statement forbids intercourse for a woman without a fixed cycle until she checks. The גמרא already explained it as being only about a woman who handles pure items. So both statements teach the same rule: only a woman who handles pure items must check.

keyTerms.meaning: one time, once already
to have marital relations
we explained it as being about (a specific case)
a woman who handles pure items

phrases.english: But שמואל already said this once!
For רבי זירא said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר יִרְמְיָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: that רבי אבא בר ירמיה said that שמואל said:
A woman who has no fixed cycle
may not have intercourse until she checks.
And we explained that as a woman who handles pure items!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new challenge against the ruling explained in Steps 20 to 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling about checking before intercourse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל gave the same rule in another statement, so this one seems repeated for no reason.

steps.title: One statement was worked out from the other
steps.stepSummary: שמואל really said only one of these statements. The other was learned from it by inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: One was said by inference from the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל did not repeat himself. He said one statement, and the other was worked out from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one of the two rulings came from שמואל's own mouth. The second was drawn from what he said and reported in his name. So there is no real repetition.

keyTerms.meaning: by implication, worked out from
its fellow, the other statement

phrases.english: One was said by inference from the other.
phrases.notes: He means שמואל only said one of them. Others drew the second from it and quoted it in his name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains how the two statements came to be: one was inferred from the other.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל said the same rule twice.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל said it once. The second version was drawn from the first.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the check is needed only for pure items. For her husband she is permitted without a check.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way: When is this said? For pure items. But for her husband she is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא limits the duty to check to a woman who handles pure items. For being with her husband, no check is needed. This matches שמואל's ruling exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? (introduces a limit on a rule)
permitted

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
When is this said?
phrases.notes: "This" means the rule that a woman must check herself.

phrases.english: For pure items,
but for her husband she is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for שמואל's ruling, now that the challenges are answered.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that only a woman handling pure items must check before intercourse.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says the check is for pure items, but she is permitted to her husband without it.

steps.title: The presumption of purity works only if he left her pure
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds a limit. She needs no check only if her husband left her presumed pure. If he left her presumed impure, she stays impure until she tells him she is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When he left her presumed pure. But if he left her presumed impure, she stays impure until she tells him, "I am pure."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and limits its own rule. Not needing a check depends on her status when the husband left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We keep assuming whatever status she last had. If she was pure when he left, we assume she is still pure. If she was impure, we assume she is still impure, until she says she is pure.

keyTerms.meaning: he left her (when he went away)
a presumption that she is impure
ritual impurity

steps.whatToRemember: A woman who does not handle pure items may be with her husband without a check, whether or not she has a fixed cycle. This works only if he left her presumed pure. If he left her presumed impure, she stays impure until she tells him she is pure.

phrases.english: When is this said?
phrases.notes: Now "this" means the rule just given, that she is permitted to her husband without a check.

phrases.english: When he left her presumed pure,
but if he left her presumed impure,
she always stays in her impurity
until she tells him, "I am pure."

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים שֶׁהִנִּיחָהּ בְּחֶזְקַת טְהוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and adds a limit to the rule in Step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She is presumed pure only if her husband left her pure. If he left her impure, she stays impure until she tells him she is pure.
